listen.description: Where the server waits for clients: ip:port like 0.0.0.0:7835, or a port alone for 0.0.0.0 (all IPv4 addresses)

public_address.description: How clients reach this server: a host name or IP (the port comes from listen), host:port, or a wss:// URL; written into the configs given to clients

websocket.description: Accept clients over WebSocket, for servers reachable only through HTTP(S)

web.description: The web proxy: one HTTPS port for websites and TLS services by name; off unless set

clients.description: Clients allowed to connect, keyed by client name

visitors.description: Visitors allowed to reach private services, keyed by visitor name

self.description: Targets this server may dial for itself, for services with client: self and visitors with reach: self

services.description: Exposed services, keyed by service name

insecure_plaintext.description: Disable encryption of forwarded data (authentication still runs)

metrics.description: Serve Prometheus metrics at /metrics; off unless set

listen.description: Address to accept WebSocket connections on, for example 127.0.0.1:7836 behind a proxy; a port alone means 0.0.0.0

path.description: URL path clients connect to, for example /tunnel

host.description: The name that leads to this server when websocket.listen is the same port as web.https, for example tunnel.example.com

tls.description: Serve wss:// directly with these PEM files instead of behind a TLS proxy

keepalive_secs.description: Seconds between keepalives on idle pooled channels, below your proxy's idle timeout

challenge.description: How Let's Encrypt checks this server's own name when it shares web.https: tls, http or dns; automatic when not set

cert.description: Certificate chain PEM file, relative to the config file, for example certs/fullchain.pem

key.description: Private key PEM file, relative to the config file, for example certs/privkey.pem

https.description: Port or ip:port for HTTPS, like 443; a port alone means every IPv4 and IPv6 address, 0.0.0.0:443 only IPv4

http.description: Port or ip:port for plain HTTP, like 80: plain-HTTP sites, the redirect to HTTPS and Let's Encrypt's HTTP check; a port alone means every IPv4 and IPv6 address

https_redirect.description: What an HTTPS site does on web.http: true sends the visitor to the same address on https:// (308), false answers plain HTTP too; sites with tls: off default to false

http2.description: true (the default) lets browsers use HTTP/2 on web.https; false keeps HTTP/1.1 only

forward_auth.description: Login services by name, each {service, path, copy_headers}; a site picks one with forward_auth: <name>, for example {authelia: {service: authelia, path: /api/authz/forward-auth}}

rate_limit.description: Default for every site: requests per second per visitor address (IPv6 per /64), bursts of twice that, 429 above

letsencrypt.description: Automatic certificates from Let's Encrypt (or another ACME server); writing it accepts Let's Encrypt's terms, for example {email: ops@example.com}

certificates.description: Shared certificate files, each for the names its hosts lists, for example [{hosts: ["*.example.com"], cert: certs/wild.pem, key: certs/wild.key}]

request_header_timeout_secs.description: Seconds a visitor may take to send a request's headers, also the keep-alive idle time; 10 when not set

idle_timeout_secs.description: Seconds without traffic before a connection is closed, WebSockets excepted; 60 when not set

redirect_names.description: Whole names, or a name and a path, with no site of their own that only redirect, for example {old.example.com: https://example.com}; temporary unless permanent: true

trusted_proxies.description: Address ranges of HTTP proxies in front of this server whose X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto are believed, for example [173.245.48.0/20]

proxy_protocol_from.description: Address ranges of TCP load balancers that start each connection with a PROXY header (v1 or v2); they must send it, nobody else may, for example [10.0.0.5/32]

access_log.description: Write one line per request to a file, or {file, format: common|json}, for example logs/access.log

request_id.description: true gives each request an X-Request-Id, sent to the app, returned to the visitor and written to the access log; false when not set

hsts.description: Default for every site: true sends Strict-Transport-Security for a year on HTTPS answers; false when not set

compress.description: Default for every site: true gzips text answers when the browser accepts it; false when not set

max_body_size.description: Default for every site: the biggest request body, like 100MB; above it the visitor gets 413; unlimited when not set

response_header_timeout_secs.description: Default for every site: seconds the app may take to start its answer, 504 after; 60 when not set

request_headers.description: Default for every site: headers set on requests to the app, Name: value; an empty value removes the header

response_headers.description: Default for every site: headers set on answers to visitors, Name: value; an empty value removes the header

error_pages.description: Default for every site: a folder with any of 404.html, 413.html, 429.html, 502.html, 503.html, 504.html and maintenance.html, relative to the config file

service.description: The service that checks each visitor, for example authelia

path.description: The path on that service that answers the check, for example /api/authz/forward-auth

copy_headers.description: Headers of the login service's answer passed on to the app, for example [Remote-User, Remote-Groups]

email.description: The account's contact address, for example ops@example.com; writing it accepts Let's Encrypt's terms

directory.description: production (the default), staging (Let's Encrypt's test service), or the directory URL of another ACME server, like https://ca.internal/acme/directory

ca.description: PEM file of the CA to trust for that ACME server, relative to the config file, for example certs/internal-ca.pem

ca_upload.description: The CA to trust for that ACME server, stored by id, for example ca-1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b

profile.description: The certificate profile to ask the CA for, for example shortlived for 6-day certificates; IP addresses always use shortlived; the CA's default when not set

dns.description: DNS providers for DNS checks (wildcards and challenge: dns), each for the domains it lists, for example [{domains: [example.com], cloudflare: {token: "${CF_TOKEN}"}}]

domains.description: The domains this provider manages; each covers itself and every name under it, for example [example.com]

cloudflare.description: Set the records through Cloudflare's API with an API token

rfc2136.description: Set the records by dynamic update signed with TSIG (RFC 2136): BIND, Knot, PowerDNS, Technitium

acme_dns.description: Set the records through an acme-dns server, reached by one CNAME per name

command.description: A program that sets the records for any provider, called as: present|cleanup _acme-challenge.NAME. VALUE

wildcards.description: Shared wildcard certificates to get through this provider, each also covering its parent name, for example ["*.example.com"]

wait_secs.description: Seconds to wait for the zone's nameservers to answer the new record before telling Let's Encrypt; 120 when not set

resolvers.description: Resolvers used only to find the zone's nameservers, for example [1.1.1.1, 9.9.9.9]; the system's when not set

token.description: The API token, from ${CF_TOKEN} or file:path; allowed Zone:Read and DNS:Edit on these zones only

server.description: The zone's primary nameserver as host:port, for example 192.168.1.2:53; the public nameservers must get the record from it

key_name.description: The TSIG key's name, as in the server's key file, for example service-key

secret.description: The TSIG secret in base64, as in the server's key file, from ${TSIG_SECRET} or file:path

algorithm.description: The TSIG key's algorithm, as in the server's key file: hmac-sha256 (the default), hmac-sha384 or hmac-sha512

api.description: The acme-dns server's address, for example https://auth.example.org

username.description: The account's user name, from ${ACMEDNS_USER} or file:path

password.description: The account's password, from ${ACMEDNS_KEY} or file:path

subdomain.description: The account's subdomain, for example d420c923-bbd7-4056-ab64-c3ca54c9b3cf

hosts.description: The names this file is used for, each listed in one entry only, for example ["*.example.com", example.com]

cert.description: Certificate chain PEM file, relative to the config file, for example certs/fullchain.pem

key.description: Private key PEM file, relative to the config file, for example certs/privkey.pem

upload.description: A certificate and its key stored by id, for example pair-1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b

to.description: Where the visitor is sent: a full URL like https://example.com/new, or a path on the same name like /new

permanent.description: true: a permanent redirect (308) that browsers remember; false (the default): a temporary one (307)

file.description: The log file, relative to the config file, for example logs/access.log

format.description: common (the default, like nginx and Apache) or json

secret.description: 256-bit secret (base64 or hex), or a list of them during rotation

max_connections.description: Maximum concurrent forwarded connections for this client

secret.description: 256-bit secret (base64 or hex), or a list of them during rotation

reach.description: Clients this visitor may reach directly, over TCP and UDP, with the targets it may pick there: any (whatever the client's allow list permits), or rules in allow-list syntax that narrow it, for example home: any, office: 192.168.150.0/25 or lab: [10.0.0.0/8:22, unix:/run/app.sock]

max_connections.description: Maximum concurrent connections for this visitor

admin.description: Let this visitor administer the server: read shows its status and config, write may also change the config

admin_from.description: Admin access only from these source IPs or CIDRs, for example [203.0.113.0/24]; any address when empty

allow.description: What this server may dial for itself: CIDR, optionally with :port or :lo-hi, or unix:/path; link-local and metadata addresses only when listed one by one

client.description: Name of the client that reaches the target

clients.description: Several clients that can each reach the target, instead of client: a name, or {name, target, weight} for another target and its share with mode: balance or ip_hash; see mode

mode.description: With several clients: failover uses the first one that is up, balance spreads new connections over all of them by weight, least_connections sends each new one to the client with the fewest open connections, ip_hash keeps each visitor address on one client, chosen by weight

health_check.description: Check that each client can reach the target, and send connections only to those that can: true, or a map with interval_secs, timeout_secs and failures

bind.description: Public address on the server: a port, or ip:port; leave it out for a private service that only visitors reach

target.description: host:port as seen from the client, or a port alone for 127.0.0.1 on the client

max_connections.description: Maximum concurrent connections for this service

visitors.description: Visitors that may reach this service

allow_from.description: Only these source IPs or CIDRs may connect, for example [203.0.113.0/24]; everyone when empty

deny_from.description: Source IPs or CIDRs that may never connect

proxy_protocol.description: Send the real source address to the target with the PROXY protocol, v1 (text) or v2 (binary); only for targets that expect it

bandwidth.description: Speed limit for each direction, shared by all connections of this service, for example 40mbit or 5MB (per second)

web.description: Make this service a website on the web proxy: a host name, a list of them, or {hosts, tls}

target.description: Where this client connects instead of the main target, for example 10.0.0.12:3000; a range must have as many ports as the main target

weight.description: Share of new connections with mode: balance, or of visitor addresses with mode: ip_hash, from 1 to 1000 (default 1); a client with weight 3 gets three times the share of one with weight 1

interval_secs.description: Seconds between checks of each client

failures.description: Failed checks in a row before a client counts as down

path.description: For a website: check with GET of this path through each client, 2xx or 3xx is up, for example /healthz; without it the check opens a TCP connection

hosts.description: Names that lead to this service: DNS names, *. wildcards of one label, or IP addresses, for example [nas.example.com]

paths.description: Only these paths on those names, each with everything below it, for example [/api]; the longest matching path wins; all paths when not set

tls.description: auto (a certificate for every name, the default with web.https), passthrough (the app does its own HTTPS; the server only reads the name), off (plain HTTP) or {cert, key} (this site's own certificate file)

https_redirect.description: true sends http:// visitors of this site to https:// (308), false answers plain HTTP too; from web.https_redirect when not set

challenge.description: How Let's Encrypt checks this site's names: tls (on web.https 443), http (on web.http 80) or dns; automatic when not set: TLS first, then HTTP

app_path.description: What the app sees in place of the matched path: paths: [/api] with app_path: /v1 sends /api/users as /v1/users; / removes the prefix

redirect_from.description: Names that redirect permanently to the first host, path and query kept, for example [www.example.com]

redirects.description: Paths on this site that redirect, for example {/old: /new} (temporary) or {/old: {to: /new, permanent: true}}

maintenance.description: true answers every request with the maintenance page (503 with Retry-After)

target_tls.description: The app speaks HTTPS: true checks its certificate against the public CAs, {ca: file} against your CA, {insecure_skip_verify: true} not at all

target_http2.description: true speaks HTTP/2 to the app: h2c, or h2 inside target_tls; for gRPC apps

basic_auth.description: Users and their password hashes, user: hash, argon2id or bcrypt (htpasswd -B)

forward_auth.description: Visitors log in at a login service first: the name of one under web.forward_auth, or true when there is only one

rate_limit.description: Requests per second per visitor address (IPv6 per /64), bursts of twice that, 429 above; from web.rate_limit when not set

client_auth.description: Only devices with a certificate signed by this CA get in, checked in the TLS handshake: {ca, crl}

hsts.description: true sends Strict-Transport-Security for a year on this site's HTTPS answers; from web.hsts when not set

compress.description: true gzips text answers when the browser accepts it; from web.compress when not set

max_body_size.description: The biggest request body, like 8GB; above it the visitor gets 413; from web.max_body_size when not set

response_header_timeout_secs.description: Seconds the app may take to start its answer, 504 after; from web.response_header_timeout_secs when not set

request_headers.description: Headers set on requests to the app, Name: value, also Host; an empty value removes the header; added to web.request_headers

response_headers.description: Headers set on answers to visitors, Name: value; an empty value removes the header; added to web.response_headers

error_pages.description: A folder with any of 404.html, 413.html, 429.html, 502.html, 503.html, 504.html and maintenance.html, relative to the config file; from web.error_pages when not set

cert.description: Certificate chain PEM file, relative to the config file, for example certs/fullchain.pem; with key, or upload instead

key.description: Private key PEM file, relative to the config file, for example certs/privkey.pem

upload.description: A certificate and its key stored by id, for example pair-1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b

ca.description: PEM file of the CA that signed the app's certificate, relative to the config file, for example certs/corp-ca.pem

ca_upload.description: The CA that signed the app's certificate, stored by id, for example ca-1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b

insecure_skip_verify.description: true: the app's certificate is not checked, for apps with a self-made certificate

ca.description: PEM file with the CA (and its intermediates) that signs the devices' certificates, relative to the config file, for example certs/devices-ca.pem

ca_upload.description: The devices' CA, stored by id, for example ca-1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b

crl.description: Revocation lists (PEM or DER) of that CA, re-read when the file changes, for example certs/devices.crl

crl_upload.description: The CA's revocation lists, stored by id, for example crl-1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b

max_handshakes.description: Concurrent connections that have not finished authenticating

max_pending.description: Connections waiting for a data channel, per client

max_peers.description: Most UDP peers one service port keeps at once; a datagram from a new peer beyond it is dropped

listen.description: Address for the metrics endpoint, for example 127.0.0.1:9100; a port alone means 127.0.0.1

remote.description: Let administrators update this server to the latest published release; off unless set
